key_insight: QISS uses low-order measurements from shallow quantum circuits as statistical guidance for classical sampling, producing strong combinatorial optimization candidates without requiring the quantum device to directly solve the problem.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a near-term hybrid workflow where noisy quantum hardware contributes scalable, error-mitigable observables while classical post-processing handles solution generation for optimization tasks.
method: Measure low-weight correlators from shallow QAOA circuits.
Use those local statistics to classically generate candidate solutions, independent of the specific optimization objective.
Optionally warm-start QAOA to further improve the quality of the sampled solutions.
evidence_signal: On MaxCut and Maximum Independent Set benchmarks, only O(N) low-order correlators were enough to beat vanilla QAOA, with p=3 QAOA correlators outperforming p=17 vanilla QAOA on 3-regular MaxCut and validation on a 54-qubit IQM Emerald device.
watch_item: The approach depends on informative low-order correlations and may require careful calibration/error mitigation to ensure the measured statistics remain reliable on hardware.
paper_title: Quantum-informed surrogate sampling for combinatorial optimization
